The matter pertains to the late submission of quarterly CMI reporting for the Registered Distributor category for the quarter October–December 2025 was comminicated by IFSCA on March 03, 2026 vide email. As a Capital Market Intermediary, the HDFC Bank IFSC Banking Unit, GIFT City is required to submit quarterly CMI reports to IFSCA within 15 days from the end of each quarter. While filing the prescribed excel based consolidated quarterly CMI return, the specific sheet relating to the Registered Distributor category was inadvertently left blank, despite all other licensed activity sheets being duly completed and submitted. The IFSCA accordingly treated the unfilled sheet as non submission for that category and advised that as per clause 8(ii) of IFSCA Circular (IFSCA-DTFA/1/2025) dated April 08, 2025, if a Regulated Entity fails to submit the periodic returns to the Authority within the specified deadline, then a late fee of $100 per month shall be paid by the RE for each such instance of default. For calculation of late fees, part of a month shall be considered as a full month. Upon receipt of the communication from the Authority, the IBU submitted the updated return containing the requisite details for the Registered Distributor category on the same day and the applicable late submission fee of USD 300 have been remitted before March 31, 2026.

operating_notes.text: Distribution network expanded to 9,700 branches and customer base reached 100 million.
Revenue per branch is ₹330 Cr versus ₹266 Cr in FY23, with close to 40% of branches less than five years old.
Business banking, the largest MSME component, grew 22.3% and corporate/wholesale advances grew about 18%.
Only 14% of customers hold time deposits with the bank, which management called an enormous penetration opportunity.

timeline.summary: HDFC Bank held its Q4 and full year FY26 earnings conference call on April 18, 2026, reporting a credit growth of 12% and deposit growth of 14.4%.
HDFC Bank announced the postal ballot voting results for the reappointment of Dr. Sunita Maheshwari as Independent Director on April 27, 2026.
HDFC Bank received RBI approval on May 6, 2026, to hold up to 9.95% aggregate share capital in ICICI Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank.
HDFC Bank Limited’s resolution via postal ballot, scrutinized by Mr. B. Narasimhan of BN & Associates, passed with majority on May 20, 2026.

HDFC Bank released the transcript of its Q2FY27 earnings conference call held on October 17, 2026.

watchlist.response: Core retail deposits are growing strongly, with less than ₹3 crores time deposit net accretion rising to 47% of total net accretion.

status_history.evidence: Wholesale deposit share rose from 17% to 20% this quarter; management said non-retail deposit costs remain elevated and the mix should normalise over the medium term.

watchlist.text: Sustainability of deposit growth and the proportion of volatile wholesale deposits.

watchlist.response: Margins are range-bound; focus is on overall return on assets (RoA) through cost efficiencies and lower credit costs.

status_history.evidence: Management reiterated margins are range-bound quarter-to-quarter and that the 40-50 bps cost-of-funds benefit is intact but will not come quickly; no margin number committed.

watchlist.text: Margin pressures from faster asset repricing versus sticky deposit rates.

watchlist.response: Adjusted for last year's HDB gains and floating/contingent provisions, growth was 9.8%; management still targets profit growth at or above balance-sheet growth over the longer term, asking analysts not to judge quarter to quarter.
watchlist.text: Earnings growth (5% reported) lagging balance sheet growth of 13-14%; can profit growth exceed it over two-three years?

watchlist.response: Management targets near the pre-merger 38%, leaning on customer unit growth (over 100 million relationships) and distribution rather than rate cuts; no date given.
watchlist.text: CASA has fallen to 34% versus peers at 40% and RBI's own report says the rate-CASA correlation is breaking down; how to get back to 40%?

watchlist.response: Evasive on quantum: "we just don't want to commit any number", promising only a significant share of the system as in 2014-15.
watchlist.text: How much FCNR(B) will the bank raise and against what benchmark?

watchlist.response: No number given; said provisions are adequate and any impact would be "some" but "nothing material", citing 1% unsecured and 5% stage-2 floors.
watchlist.text: Quantify the one-time and ongoing credit cost impact of moving to ECL

watchlist.response: The question was not answered; the CFO moved to the ECL question.
watchlist.text: Why is interest on balances with RBI and others growing sharply QoQ; any one-off?
